title: 7-Day Amalfi Coast Itinerary: Sorrento · Pompeii · Positano · Amalfi · Capri · Ravello
description: The full Amalfi Coast experience — no rushing. Split your base between Sorrento and the coast for the perfect mix of ruins, clifftop villages, island escapes, and long Italian lunches by the sea.

activities.name: Arrive Naples & Transfer to Sorrento
activities.description: Land at Naples airport and catch the Campania Express train to Sorrento (book ahead — comfier and faster than the Circumvesuviana). Drop bags at your hotel near Piazza Tasso.
details: 💡 Campania Express: ~€15, reserved seats, 70 min
💡 Circumvesuviana: ~€4, standing room, 75 min but more frequent

activities.name: Explore Sorrento Old Town
activities.description: Wander the narrow streets off Corso Italia. Visit the Vallone dei Mulini — a hauntingly beautiful abandoned mill in a deep ravine right in the town center. Pop into a limoncello shop for a free tasting (they're everywhere).
details: 📸 Vallone dei Mulini is best photographed from Via Fuorimura
🍋 Limonoro on Corso Italia has excellent limoncello tastings

activities.name: Sunset at Villa Comunale & Dinner
activities.description: Head to Villa Comunale park for golden-hour views over the Bay of Naples with Vesuvius in the background. For dinner, try Inn Bufalito for incredible buffalo mozzarella dishes or Ristorante Museo Caruso for a Michelin-quality experience.
details: 🍽️ Inn Bufalito — mozzarella-focused menu, €15–25 mains
🍽️ Ristorante Museo Caruso — fine dining, reserve ahead

activities.name: Pompeii Archaeological Park
activities.description: Take the early Circumvesuviana to Pompei Scavi (30 min from Sorrento). Arrive by 9am to beat the heat and crowds. Allow 3–4 hours for the highlights: the Forum, House of the Faun, amphitheater, Garden of the Fugitives, and the remarkably preserved thermopolium (ancient fast-food counter).
details: 🎫 Book tickets online at ticketone.it — €18/person
💡 Grab the free map at the entrance — the site is massive
👟 Wear sturdy shoes — ancient Roman streets are uneven cobblestone
💡 Hire a guide at the gate (~€15pp in a group) for fascinating context

activities.name: Sorrento Beach & Old Town
activities.description: Return to Sorrento and head to Bagni della Regina Giovanna — a natural swimming pool in ancient Roman ruins, a 25-minute walk from the center. The crystal-clear cove is surrounded by the remains of a 1st-century villa. Then explore Sorrento's shopping streets for custom leather sandals and ceramic souvenirs.
details: 🏊 Bagni della Regina Giovanna — free, bring your own towel
👡 Custom sandals made while-you-wait on Via San Cesareo (~€30–50)

activities.name: Farewell Sorrento Dinner
activities.description: Last night in Sorrento. Grab aperitivo at Fauno Bar on Piazza Tasso (the main square) for prime people-watching, then dinner at O'Parrucchiano La Favorita — a stunning garden restaurant since 1868, serving classic Sorrentine cuisine under lemon trees.
details: 🍽️ O'Parrucchiano — try the gnocchi alla sorrentina, €18
🍸 Fauno Bar — Aperol Spritz + people-watching from the terrace

activities.name: Ferry to Amalfi
activities.description: Take the morning ferry from Sorrento to Amalfi (seasonal, ~€12, 75 min). The ferry route offers jaw-dropping views of the entire coastline — sit on the right side for the best photo ops. Check into your accommodation in Amalfi town.
details: ⛴️ Ferries run April–October, check Travelmar or Alilauro schedules
💡 Alternative: SITA bus via Positano (cheaper but winding, ~90 min)

activities.name: Amalfi Cathedral & Town Center
activities.description: Explore the Duomo di Amalfi (Cathedral of St. Andrew), a stunning 9th-century cathedral with Arab-Norman architecture. Climb the 62 steps for close-up views of the ornate mosaic facade. Inside, visit the Chiostro del Paradiso — a 13th-century cloister with Moorish arches and peaceful gardens. Follow the coastal path (10-minute walk) to Atrani — the Amalfi Coast's smallest and most authentic village. Where Amalfi gets cruise-ship crowds, Atrani stays blissfully local. Sit in Piazza Umberto I, watch old men play cards, and grab a coffee at one of the bars lining the tiny square.
details: ⛪ Duomo — €3 entry, includes crypt and cloister
📸 Best photos of the cathedral from Piazza del Duomo below
💎 Atrani is the hidden gem of the Amalfi Coast — fewer tourists, better vibes
🏖️ Atrani beach is smaller but less crowded than Amalfi's

activities.name: Aperitivo & Seafood Dinner
activities.description: Sunset aperitivo at A'Paranza in Atrani, then walk back to Amalfi for dinner at Trattoria da Gemma — a family-run institution since 1872 known for its zuppa di pesce (fish stew) and handmade scialatielli pasta with seafood.
details: 🍽️ Trattoria da Gemma — reserve 2–3 days ahead, mains €18–30
🍽️ Lo Smeraldino — casual waterfront pizza if Gemma is full, €10–15

activities.name: Path of the Gods Hike
activities.description: Take the early SITA bus from Amalfi to Bomerano (Agerola) — the trailhead for the legendary Sentiero degli Dei (Path of the Gods). This spectacular clifftop trail runs 7.8km along sheer cliffs 500m above the sea with non-stop panoramic views of the coast, Capri, and the Li Galli islands. The trail ends in Nocelle, where you descend 1,700 steps to Positano.
details: 🥾 Difficulty: Moderate. Allow 2.5–3 hours one way
🕐 Start by 8am to avoid midday heat and afternoon crowds
💡 Hike west→east (Bomerano→Nocelle) so the views are always in front of you
🧃 Bring water and snacks — no services on the trail
👟 Sturdy shoes essential — some rocky/narrow sections near cliffs

activities.name: Positano Exploration
activities.description: After descending from Nocelle, you'll arrive in the upper part of Positano. Wind your way down through the colorful bougainvillea-draped streets to the beach. Skip the main Spiaggia Grande (overcrowded) and head left to Fornillo Beach — smaller, more local, and with better beach clubs. Take the free shuttle boat from Spiaggia Grande to Da Adolfo — a legendary, no-frills beach restaurant only accessible by sea. Fresh grilled fish, mozzarella on lemon leaves, and house rosé with your feet practically in the water.
details: 🏖️ Fornillo Beach — sun loungers ~€15–20, much calmer than the main beach
📸 Best photo spot: the viewpoint on Via Positanesi d'America
🍽️ Da Adolfo — cash only, mains €15–25, look for the red fish flag
⛵ Free shuttle boat runs every 30 min from the main beach jetty

activities.name: Positano Sunset & Return
activities.description: Golden hour in Positano is pure magic. Watch the sunset from the beach or splurge on a cocktail at Le Sirenuse Hotel's champagne bar — arguably the best view on the entire coast. Then catch the evening ferry back to Amalfi.
details: 🍸 Le Sirenuse Franco's Bar — cocktails €20–25, worth every cent for the view
⛴️ Last ferry to Amalfi typically 7:30pm — check seasonal schedule

activities.name: Ferry to Capri & Marina Grande
activities.description: Catch the morning ferry from Amalfi to Capri (~€22, 80 min via Positano). Arrive at Marina Grande and take the funicular up to Capri town (€2.20). Start at the Giardini di Augusto for the most famous viewpoint on the island — overlooking the Faraglioni sea stacks and the serpentine Via Krupp below.
details: ⛴️ First ferry ~8:30am, book day before in peak season
🎫 Giardini di Augusto — €1 entry, tiny price for an iconic view
📸 Via Krupp is currently closed to walkers but stunning from above

activities.name: Anacapri & Monte Solaro
activities.description: Take the bus to Anacapri (quieter, less glamorous than Capri town). Ride the single-seat chairlift to Monte Solaro (589m) — the island's highest point with 360° views of the entire Bay of Naples, Amalfi Coast, and on clear days, the mountains of Calabria. The 12-minute ride is thrilling and unforgettable.
details: 🚡 Chairlift — €12 round trip, opens at 9:30am
💡 The open-air chairlift has no safety bar — not for the faint of heart!
🍝 Lunch in Anacapri at Il Riccio — Michelin-starred seafood on the cliffs

activities.name: Capri Town & Optional Blue Grotto
activities.description: Return to Capri town and stroll the Piazzetta (the tiny, glamorous main square), browse the designer boutiques, and wander to the Arco Naturale — a dramatic natural stone arch. If you want to try the Blue Grotto, take a boat from Marina Grande (but be warned: long waits, expensive, and it closes with even slight waves).
details: 🔵 Blue Grotto — €18 entry + €15 rowboat, often 1-2 hour wait
💡 Skip the Blue Grotto if time is tight — Monte Solaro + Faraglioni are better
🍨 Buonocore gelateria on Via Vittorio Emanuele — best gelato on the island

activities.name: Return to Amalfi
activities.description: Catch the evening ferry back to Amalfi. Have a casual dinner at Lo Smeraldino on the Amalfi waterfront — good pizza and pasta without the fine-dining price tag.
details: ⛴️ Last ferry Capri→Amalfi around 5:30–6:30pm depending on season

activities.name: Bus to Ravello
activities.description: Take the SITA bus from Amalfi up to Ravello (25 min, €1.30). This hilltop town sits 350m above the sea and has been a magnet for artists, writers, and musicians for centuries. Wagner, Greta Garbo, Virginia Woolf — they all came here for the same reason: the views are absurd. Start at Villa Rufolo — 13th-century gardens that inspired Wagner's Parsifal, now host the famous Ravello Festival concerts on a stage suspended over the sea. Then walk 10 minutes to Villa Cimbrone for the legendary Terrazza dell'Infinito (Terrace of Infinity) — a belvedere lined with marble busts overlooking the entire coastline. It's the single most photographed viewpoint on the Amalfi Coast.
details: 🚌 Buses run every 30 min from Amalfi's Piazza Flavio Gioia
🎫 Villa Rufolo — €10, Villa Cimbrone — €10
📸 Terrace of Infinity is best in morning light before 11am
🎵 Ravello Festival (June–Sept) — buy concert tickets months ahead

activities.name: Lunch with a View
activities.description: Lunch at Ristorante Salvatore in Ravello — family-run with a terrace overlooking the entire coastline. Their homemade pasta with lemon cream sauce is legendary. Alternatively, Cumpa Cosimo is a more casual local favorite with generous portions.
details: 🍽️ Ristorante Salvatore — mains €16–28, terrace seating essential
🍽️ Cumpa Cosimo — hearty portions, €12–20 mains, book for lunch

activities.name: Emerald Grotto (Grotta dello Smeraldo)
activities.description: Bus back toward Amalfi and stop at Conca dei Marini for the Emerald Grotto — a sea cave where sunlight filters through an underwater opening, casting an ethereal emerald-green glow on the water. You descend by elevator or stairs to small boats that take you inside.
details: 💎 €5 entry + €5 boat ride, 15-minute visit
💡 Less hyped than the Blue Grotto but more accessible and no crazy waits

activities.name: Sunset Dinner in Praiano
activities.description: Continue by bus to Praiano — a quieter, more residential town between Amalfi and Positano. Praiano faces due west, making it the best sunset spot on the coast. Have dinner at Kasai — an intimate terrace restaurant where you'll watch the sun melt into the Tyrrhenian Sea with a glass of local Furore wine.
details: 🍽️ Kasai — modern Italian, €20–35 mains, book sunset table
🌅 Praiano sunsets are the best on the coast — it faces directly west
🚌 Last bus Praiano→Amalfi around 10pm

activities.name: Optional: Private Boat Tour
activities.description: If budget allows, splurge on a private boat tour along the coast (€150–300 for a small boat, split among passengers). You'll see the coast from its most magical angle — hidden coves, sea caves, the Faraglioni from the water, and swimming stops in impossibly blue water. Many tours depart from Amalfi at 9am and return by 1pm.
details: ⛵ Book through your hotel or try Amalfi Coast Boat Tours
💡 A group of 4–6 makes this very affordable per person
🏊 Bring swimsuit and towel — you'll want to jump in

activities.name: Final Amalfi Stroll & Lunch
activities.description: Last walk through Amalfi. Pick up handmade paper at the Paper Museum (Amalfi was a major medieval paper producer), grab limoncello souvenirs, and have a final lunch at La Pansa — the pastry shop/cafe on Piazza Duomo since 1830.
details: 🏛️ Paper Museum (Museo della Carta) — €5, fascinating 30-min visit
🍰 La Pansa — try the sfogliatella and delizia al limone
🍋 Best limoncello: Antichi Sapori d'Amalfi on Via Supportico Ferrari

activities.name: Transfer to Naples Airport
activities.description: Ferry from Amalfi to Salerno (35 min, €8) then bus or train to Naples airport. Alternatively, ferry to Sorrento then Circumvesuviana to Naples. Allow 3 hours for the full journey. For a stress-free option, book a private transfer (€100–120).
details: 💡 Amalfi→Salerno ferry is the most reliable connection
🚆 Salerno→Naples airport: bus (Buonotourist, ~€8) or train+taxi
💡 Private transfer: book through your hotel, ~€100–120 to NAP airport
